title: Wiring the house to the bus
tasks: wire_home(target, devs): subscribe handlers for motion, motion_clear and temperature on whatever bus and devices are passed in
The thermostat handler publishes a heating event, but only when the heating state changes
Count visits from motion events and return the list of unsubscribe handles
Connect the hub's own bus and devices, then drive the house from the scene and read the log
explanation: wire_home takes the bus and devices as parameters, so the same function wires the real hub and the throwaway objects the tests create. The handlers are short because the resilient bus catches their failures: a reading with no value becomes one KeyError in the dead-letter box instead of defensive code everywhere. Publishing heating only on change keeps the log meaningful, and returning the handles gives the caller a clean way to undo everything.

hints.title: The motion handlers
hints.content: Inside wire_home define def on_motion(event): sensor = devs.get(f"{event.payload.get('room')}_motion"); if sensor is not None: sensor.execute("trigger"). on_motion_clear is the same with "clear". For visits, check room in visit_counts before calling count_visit(room).

hints.title: The thermostat handler
hints.content: thermostat = devs.get("thermostat"); return if it is None. Remember was_heating = thermostat.heating, call thermostat.execute("measure", event.payload["value"]), and if thermostat.heating != was_heating emit target.emit("heating", {"on": thermostat.heating}).

hints.title: Returning handles
hints.content: End wire_home with return [target.subscribe("motion", on_motion), target.subscribe("motion", on_visit), target.subscribe("motion_clear", on_motion_clear), target.subscribe("temperature", on_temperature)]. Outside the function: wiring = wire_home(bus, devices).

checks.prompt: Which event name follows the "name what happened" convention?
checks.explanation: Events are facts (`heating` changed, `motion` was seen). Names like `turn_on_hall_light` are commands: they presume exactly one consequence and tie the publisher to the receiver.

checks.prompt: `on_temperature` reads `event.payload["value"]` without checking that the key exists. Why is that acceptable here?

options: The resilient bus catches and records the failure, so the handler can stay short and fail fast
The payload is validated by the scene before sending

checks.explanation: Handlers trust their input; the boundary (the bus) deals with the rare bad event by filing it as a dead letter. Defensive checks in every handler would duplicate that work.
